items.title: Top 5 Coldest Places in the Universe (#1 Is Colder Than Space) #shorts
items.description:
The five coldest places we know, from Uranus to a nebula colder than empty space. #2 is on our own Moon. Full video on the channel: "Why Is Space Black If There Are Billions of Stars? (Olbers' Paradox)".

Sources
- NASA Science, Uranus: minimum atmospheric temperature 49 K (−224 °C), the coldest planetary atmosphere in the solar system
- NASA Science, Pluto: surface temperatures of about −232 to −223 °C; nitrogen ice on the surface
- NASA Science, Triton: surface about −235 °C measured by Voyager 2 (1989); active geyser-like plumes
- NASA LRO / Diviner (Paige et al., 2009): Hermite crater floor about 26 K (≈ −247 °C), the coldest temperature measured in the solar system
- ESA / NASA Hubble and ALMA (Sahai et al., 2013): Boomerang Nebula about 1 K, about 5,000 light-years away, colder than the 2.7 K cosmic microwave background
- Own calculations: kelvin = °C + 273.15

Visuals and animations are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #cold #astronomy

items.title: What If Jupiter Became a Star? It Would Need 80 Jupiters
items.description:
Turn Jupiter into a star, step by step. It would need about 80 times its mass, it would barely change size, and from Earth it would shine like a red full Moon. The Sun would start to wobble almost out to Mercury's orbit, the outer planets would be in danger, and Jupiter's four big moons would end up inside the new star. And the twist: the star that used to be Jupiter would outlive the Sun by trillions of years.

Chapters
0:00 A second sun over Earth
0:34 Step 1: Jupiter isn't a failed star
1:32 Step 2: add mass (it doesn't grow)
1:50 13 Jupiters: a brown dwarf
2:26 About 80 Jupiters: a star
2:42 A real star smaller than Jupiter
3:09 Step 3: where's the mass?
3:28 Step 4: the new sky
3:52 Step 5: the Sun starts to wobble
4:56 Step 6: which planets survive
5:18 What happens to Jupiter's moons
6:29 Fiction vs physics
6:49 The twist: it outlives the Sun
7:11 The full recipe
7:33 Next episode

Sources
- NASA Planetary Fact Sheets: Jupiter mass 1.898 × 10^27 kg (317.8 Earth masses, about 1/1,048 of the Sun), radius 71,492 km, distance 5.2 AU, orbit 11.86 years; masses of the other planets
- NASA Science, Jupiter: made mostly of hydrogen and helium; core temperature estimated at about 24,000 °C (43,000 °F)
- Sky at Night Magazine / Space.com: Jupiter is not a failed star; it would need roughly 75 to 80 times more mass to fuse hydrogen and become a red dwarf
- NASA / EarthSky, brown dwarfs: deuterium fusion begins near 13 Jupiter masses; brown dwarfs are about the size of Jupiter
- NASA / JPL WISE (2013), Luhman: Luhman 16 AB, the closest known brown dwarfs, about 6.5 light-years away
- University of Cambridge (2017), von Boetticher et al., Astronomy & Astrophysics: EBLM J0555-57Ab, about 85 Jupiter masses, radius about 0.84 Jupiter's, comparable to Saturn
- Raghavan et al. (2010), Astrophysical Journal Supplement: about 44% of nearby Sun-like stars have at least one stellar companion
- Holman & Wiegert (1999), Astronomical Journal: stability limit for planets orbiting one star of a binary
- Laughlin, Bodenheimer & Adams (1997), Astrophysical Journal, "The End of the Main Sequence": the smallest red dwarfs live for trillions of years; NASA: the Sun's lifetime is about 10 billion years
- Pearl & Conrath (1991), Journal of Geophysical Research (Voyager data): Jupiter emits about 1.67 times the energy it absorbs from the Sun
- Arthur C. Clarke, "2010: Odyssey Two" (1982): Jupiter ignited into the small sun Lucifer
- NASA Europa Clipper: Europa likely hides a global salt-water ocean beneath its ice
- Own calculations (Python): 80 Jupiter masses = 0.076 solar masses; Sun–Jupiter barycentre today about 1.07 solar radii from the Sun's centre, with 80× the mass about 0.37 AU (Mercury orbits at 0.39 AU), period about 11.4 years; assuming a luminosity of about 0.0001 Suns, at 4.2 AU it would reach about magnitude −13.6 (full Moon −12.7) and warm Earth by about 0.0004 °C; Galilean moon orbits shrinking as 1/mass (Io about 5,300 km, Callisto about 23,500 km from the centre) vs a star radius of about 60,000 km; with instant growth Callisto's closest approach about 11,800 km; Holman & Wiegert stability limit about 2.1 AU; reflex speed of the Sun today about 12.5 m/s, with an 80-Jupiter companion about 960 m/s; all other planets together about 0.4 Jupiter masses

—

items.title: This Star Fits Inside Jupiter. It Weighs 85 Jupiters. #shorts
items.description:
A real star, EBLM J0555-57Ab, drawn to scale: 85 times Jupiter's mass, but small enough to fit inside Jupiter, about the size of Saturn. Full video on the channel: "What If Jupiter Became a Star? It Would Need 80 Jupiters".

Sources
- University of Cambridge (July 2017), von Boetticher et al., Astronomy & Astrophysics: EBLM J0555-57Ab, about 85 Jupiter masses, slightly larger than Saturn, about 600 light-years away, orbiting a Sun-like star; just massive enough to fuse hydrogen
- NASA Planetary Fact Sheets: Jupiter radius 71,492 km, Saturn radius 58,232 km
- Own calculation: star radius ≈ 0.84 Jupiter radii ≈ 59,000 km, so it fits inside Jupiter's disc

Visuals and animations are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.

items.title: If Jupiter Became a Star, Its 4 Big Moons Would End Up INSIDE It #shorts
items.description:
Make Jupiter 80 times heavier and its moons' orbits shrink about 80 times. Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto would all end up inside the new star. Full video on the channel: "What If Jupiter Became a Star? It Would Need 80 Jupiters".

Sources
- NASA Planetary Fact Sheets: Jupiter mass 1.898 × 10^27 kg (317.8 Earth masses, about 1/1,048 of the Sun), radius 71,492 km, distance 5.2 AU, orbit 11.86 years; masses of the other planets
- NASA Science, Jupiter's moons: Io 421,700 km, Europa 671,034 km, Ganymede 1,070,412 km, Callisto 1,882,709 km from Jupiter
- Own calculation: with slow mass growth orbit size × mass stays constant, so orbits shrink about 80×; the new star's radius is about 60,000 km

Visuals and animations are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
